answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may influence decisions, then randomly audit claims and confiscate the bond when linked identities coordinate dishonestly. A sybil attacker must therefore split real capital across many accounts and keep it locked, rather than minting costless names; evading detection risks losing that capital. The bond could be denominated in copper, while a forge of accounts still cannot forge collateral, and a plume of cheap identities becomes expensive to sustain.
